title: Extracting Coding Sequences from Plants Without Genome Data
author: Kaia Kukk
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.btxwnppe
materials: RevertAid H Minus First Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit

Try to find sequence that has melting temperature (Tm) of at least 54 °C and low degeneracy. Calculate both the lowest and highest potential Tm. Design the primers such a way that the amplified sequence will be approximately 200-500 bp long (both forward and reverse primer is needed). The lower the degeneracy the longer can the distance between the primers be. We used Tm calculator at Thermo Fisher web page for Phusion polymerase. We have successfully used a primer mix the degeneracy of which was 1152.

steps.title: Collect and store plant material
steps.instruction: Harvest fresh plant tissue, immediately freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –70 °C or lower until use.

steps.title: Extract total RNA
steps.instruction: For simple green leaves use Protocol 1 (DNA‑free RNA isolation for Arabidopsis). For anthocyanin‑ or polysaccharide‑rich tissues (e.g., bilberry berries, cornflower flowers) use the Spectrum Plant Total RNA Kit following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Assess RNA quality
steps.instruction: Run a native agarose gel and measure OD260/OD280; acceptable values are ≈2.0 (e.g., 2.04, 1.71).

steps.title: Synthesize first‑strand cDNA
steps.instruction: Use the RevertAid H Minus First Strand cDNA Synthesis Kit according to the supplier’s protocol.

steps.title: Retrieve homologous protein sequences
steps.instruction: Search NCBI (Protein or Nucleotide) and UniProt for orthologous proteins; also check KEGG and BRENDA for alternative names. Save both nucleotide and amino‑acid sequences together with their accession numbers.

steps.title: Align sequences and select conserved residues
steps.instruction: Align the retrieved amino‑acid sequences with MegAlign (DNAStar), COBALT, Clustal Omega or any other MSA tool. Identify conserved regions that contain amino acids encoded by a small number of codons (Met, Trp, Asn, Asp, Cys, Gln, Glu, His, Lys, Phe, Tyr).

steps.title: Design degenerate primers and check dimers
steps.instruction: From the conserved regions design degenerate primers (e.g., AAD GCN TGY GTN GAH ATG GAY CAR AA, 1152 possible sequences). Verify primer‑dimer formation on the Thermo Fisher website and avoid dimers and 3′‑end degeneracy.

steps.title: Perform touchdown PCR with degenerate primers
steps.instruction: Prepare a 50 µl reaction containing 2 µl cDNA, 0.2 mM dNTPs, 2 µM degenerate sense primer, 2 µM degenerate antisense primer, 1× HF buffer, 1 U Phusion High‑Fidelity DNA Polymerase (2 U/µl) and water to volume. Run the following program: Initial denaturation 98 °C 30 s; 8 touchdown cycles of 98 °C 10 s, annealing 65 °C → 58 °C → 52 °C each for 30 s, extension 72 °C 20 s; followed by 25 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, annealing 52 °C 30 s, extension 72 °C 20 s; final extension 72 °C 300 s; hold 4 °C.

steps.title: Verify PCR products and purify fragments
steps.instruction: Run the PCR mix on a 1 % agarose gel containing ethidium bromide. Excise bands of the expected size and purify with the GeneJET Gel Extraction and DNA Cleanup Micro Kit.

steps.title: Ligate fragments into pJET1.2 vector
steps.instruction: Ligate purified PCR fragments into the blunt‑ended pJET1.2 vector using T4 DNA ligase at room temperature for 1–2 h.

steps.title: Transform E. coli and plate colonies
steps.instruction: Transform ligation mix into E. coli DH5α, spread on LB agar containing ampicillin (50 µg ml⁻¹) using sterile glass beads, and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Screen colonies by colony PCR
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony with a toothpick or yellow pipette tip, smear onto the inner wall of a 0.2 ml PCR tube, and add 20 µl PCR mix: 2.5 mM MgCl₂, 0.25 mM dNTPs, 1× Taq buffer, 0.5 µM pJET1.2 forward primer, 0.5 µM reverse primer, 0.2 µl Taq polymerase (1 U). PCR program: 95 °C 5 min; 30 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 60 °C 30 s, 72 °C 1 min kb⁻¹; final extension 72 °C 200 s. Run products on an agarose gel; the correct insert appears as the expected size plus 120 bp.

steps.title: Grow positive clone and miniprep plasmid
steps.instruction: Inoculate 3–5 ml LB+Amp (50 µg ml⁻¹) with a positive colony, grow overnight, and isolate plasmid DNA using the GeneJET Plasmid Miniprep Kit.

steps.title: Sequence cloned fragments
steps.instruction: Submit the miniprep DNA for Sanger sequencing with the pJET1.2 forward and reverse primers.

steps.title: Design specific sense primer(s)
steps.instruction: Using the obtained fragment sequences, design sense primer(s) with a melting temperature (Tm) of ≥62 °C; one primer may be sufficient for ~1 kb amplification.

steps.title: Conduct 3′ RACE to extend 3′ end
steps.instruction: Perform reverse transcription with RevertAid H Minus reverse transcriptase and the 3‑RACE‑CDS primer (5’‑AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTACTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTVN‑3’). Then run conventional PCR using the specific sense primer and the primer 5’‑AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGT‑3’ (Tm = 67 °C).

steps.title: Clone and sequence 3′ RACE products
steps.instruction: Purify the 3′ RACE PCR bands, ligate into pJET1.2, transform E. coli, screen colonies as before, miniprep plasmids and sequence with pJET1.2 primers.

steps.title: Design specific antisense primer(s)
steps.instruction: From the combined 5′ and 3′ fragment sequences design antisense primers with Tm ≥ 62 °C; include an outer and an inner primer spaced ≈100 bp apart.

steps.title: Perform 5′ RACE to extend 5′ end
steps.instruction: Use either the SMARTer RACE 5′/3′ Kit or the FirstChoice RLM‑RACE Kit. Carry out two rounds of PCR with gene‑specific outer and inner antisense primers together with the kit‑provided adapter primers. Expect up to ~0.5 kb 5′ sequence.

steps.title: Clone and sequence 5′ RACE products
steps.instruction: Purify the 5′ RACE bands, ligate into pJET1.2, transform, screen colonies, miniprep plasmids and sequence as described for earlier fragments.

steps.title: Assemble full‑length coding sequence
steps.instruction: Align the 5′ and 3′ RACE sequences, identify overlapping regions, merge them into a contiguous coding sequence and locate open reading frames.

steps.title: Amplify full‑length ORF with designed primers
steps.instruction: Design primers annealing to the 5′ and 3′ ends of the assembled ORF (Tm ≥ 62 °C) and amplify the full‑length product using the cDNA from step 3 or the 3′‑RACE cDNA from step 16.

steps.title: Clone, verify, and sequence full‑length product
steps.instruction: Purify the full‑length PCR fragment from a gel, ligate into pJET1.2, transform E. coli, screen colonies, miniprep plasmids and sequence with pJET1.2 primers to confirm the complete coding sequence.

steps.title: Deposit final sequence in public repository
steps.instruction: Submit the verified coding sequence to a public database such as GenBank and/or PlutoF.
